### Modifications Summary

#### Modifications in Each File:

1. **`drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/xsk/tx.c`**
   - Added a check to prevent multiple NOP WQE postings by introducing a new state `MLX5E_SQ_STATE_PENDING_XSK_TX`. If this state is already set, the function returns early, avoiding the triggering of an IRQ multiple times.

2. **`drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en.h`**
   - Introduced a new enumeration value `MLX5E_SQ_STATE_PENDING_XSK_TX` to represent the pending state for XSK transmission.

3. **`drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_txrx.c`**
   - Modified the call to `mlx5e_poll_ico_cq` to check its return value. If nothing was polled, it prevents clearing the pending state, thus avoiding queueing more WQEs and potential overflow.

4. **`drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_rx.c`**
   - Changed the return type of `mlx5e_poll_ico_cq` from `void` to `int`, allowing it to return a value indicating whether any work was polled. This change is crucial for the logic in `en_txrx.c`.

#### Relationships Between Modifications:

- The addition of the `MLX5E_SQ_STATE_PENDING_XSK_TX` state in `en.h` is directly related to the changes in `en/xsk/tx.c`, where it is used to prevent multiple IRQ triggers during XSK wakeup. This state management ensures that only one NOP WQE is posted at a time, thus preventing overflows in the XSK ICOSQ.

- The modification in `en_txrx.c` to check the return value of `mlx5e_poll_ico_cq` is dependent on the changes made in `en_rx.c`, where the function now returns an integer. This relationship allows the system to determine if any work was polled and manage the pending state accordingly, further preventing the overflow issue.

Overall, these modifications work together to enhance the handling of XSK wakeup requests, ensuring that the system remains stable under high load conditions.

   - Added a check to see if the `MLX5E_SQ_STATE_PENDING_XSK_TX` flag is already set before proceeding with the wakeup process. If it is set, the function returns early to prevent multiple IRQ triggers.

        Root cause:
        The bug is caused by the `mlx5e_trigger_irq` function being called multiple times in quick succession when the application floods the driver with wakeup requests. This leads to multiple NOP Work Queue Entries (WQEs) being posted to the XSK ICOSQ, which can overflow due to the increased queue size and the inability to process the entries quickly enough.
        
        Commit message:
        net/mlx5e: Don't trigger IRQ multiple times on XSK wakeup to
 avoid WQ overruns

XSK wakeup function triggers NAPI by posting a NOP WQE to a special XSK
ICOSQ. When the application floods the driver with wakeup requests by
calling sendto() in a certain pattern that ends up in mlx5e_trigger_irq,
the XSK ICOSQ may overflow.

Multiple NOPs are not required and won't accelerate the process, so
avoid posting a second NOP if there is one already on the way. This way
we also avoid increasing the queue size (which might not help anyway).

Fixes: db05815b36cb ("net/mlx5e: Add XSK zero-copy support")
Signed-off-by: Maxim Mikityanskiy <maximmi@mellanox.com>
Reviewed-by: Tariq Toukan <tariqt@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: Saeed Mahameed <saeedm@mellanox.com>

        diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/xsk/tx.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/xsk/tx.c
index fe2d596cb361..3bcdb5b2fc20 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/xsk/tx.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/xsk/tx.c
@@ -33,6 +33,9 @@ int mlx5e_xsk_wakeup(struct net_device *dev, u32 qid, u32 flags)
 		if (unlikely(!test_bit(MLX5E_SQ_STATE_ENABLED, &c->xskicosq.state)))
 			return 0;
 
+		if (test_and_set_bit(MLX5E_SQ_STATE_PENDING_XSK_TX, &c->xskicosq.state))
+			return 0;
+
 		spin_lock(&c->xskicosq_lock);
 		mlx5e_trigger_irq(&c->xskicosq);
 		spin_unlock(&c->xskicosq_lock);
